rows.medi_said: Ayan, Ayan is sick. / خطيبتي, شوي, Ayan.
rows.why: He used masculine عيان for his fiancée; Amal echoed the feminine عيانة (02:00 and 02:23) and he took it ('Yeah, Ayana').
rows.english: my fiancée is a bit sick
rows.r3_why: Her echo gives the feminine and he repeats it - recast.

rows.why: Amal recast his order (verb with -ha before راسها) to راسها بيوجع twice and he repeated it back ('He rasa biwaja').

rows.medi_said: I don't know how to say cough. She has a cough.
rows.amal_said: They say but كح. I say كحة.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked for 'cough' and Amal supplied كحة.
rows.r3_why: Real didn't-know, she supplied the word.

rows.why: MSA الآن for 'now'; sheet row 'now | Halla | هلا | hala'; Amal only said 'إحنا group. أها.' and let it pass.
rows.r3_why: Real: he used MSA الآن where her sheet has هلا; she gave no signal, so vocab-B.

rows.amal_said: You're worried about. You're worried from. ... Men، men.
rows.why: He reached for لـ for 'worried about fire'; Amal said worried takes من ('Men, men') and he said من نار.

rows.amal_said: no. There's another word for that.
rows.right: (another verb for a fire starting; not given)
rows.why: He offered يبدأ for a fire starting; Amal said no, there is another word (she did not supply it).

rows.medi_said: do I know how to say taking care or like caring for?
rows.why: He asked how to say 'take care of'; Amal supplied ديرت بالي.
Missing على after دير بال (Amal 11:45 'بدير بالي takes على') and missing -i on بال; her recast بالي على خطيبتي. He repeated the على-less form at 11:35 (same slip, one row).
rows.english: I took care of my fiancée.

rows.amal_said: دير بالك is actually the command form.
rows.why: Asked for another example he produced ديري باليك; Amal gave دير بالك and named it as the command form (and بالك, not باليك).

rows.medi_said: الدرس إنه إنتي... / خلينا نعمل الدرس إنه، إنه تفتتلي.
rows.why: 'The lesson that you planned' needs اللي, not إنه (he said so at 15:13: 'the lesson that you planned'); Amal only asked what he meant, no fix voiced. Said first at 14:42, again at 15:00.
rows.english: let's do the lesson that you planned
rows.r3_why: Real relative-clause slip; her كيف يعني is not understanding, not a fix, so grammar-B. Kept at the first occurrence (14:42); D2 merged here.

rows.why: After خلينا the verb is a bare present; he used past عملنا, Amal said نعمل and he repeated it.
تفتتلي is not a word for 'you planned' (he says so at 15:13); Amal asked كيف يعني and moved on; best reading خططتي.
rows.r3_challenge: تفتتلي is unreadable engine text (he meant 'you planned', said in English at 15:13); Amal's كيف يعني only shows she did not understand. The wrong word cannot be read from the transcript - audio check.

rows.medi_said: أنا راح، um، عمله، uh، قلات كتير بس.
rows.amal_said: Okay، يعني you're up to trying without.
rows.why: ra7 + bare verb needs the person prefix (أعمله); engine wrote عمله after a pause. Low: the أ can be swallowed by the engine. Amal let it pass.
rows.english: I'll do it, (with) a lot of mistakes
rows.r3_why: Plausible B13 slip with no signal; low because the dropped أ could be the engine.

rows.medi_said: Oh, is it، أسف؟ ... oh my gosh, what was sky? ... أنا نسيتو.
rows.amal_said: No، عصافير is birds. ... It's a girl's name ... سما.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he guessed أسف (bird) for 'sky', Amal said no, he said he forgot and she supplied سما (sheet 'sky | Sama | سما').
rows.r3_why: One didn't-know row for sky; D3 merged here.

rows.medi_said: When, when do you look at the sky? When do you watch the sky?
rows.amal_said: No، امتى بتتطلع على الشمس would be when do you watch the sky؟ امتى الشمس بتطلع؟
rows.right: When does the sun go up / rise (بتطلع)
rows.why: Listening: he understood her امتى الشمس بتطلع as 'when do you watch the sky'; Amal said no, it means when does the sun rise.

rows.medi_said: أنا نسي تلك الكلمة بس سجر. سجر؟
rows.amal_said: فجر. You could have just said الصبح بكير
rows.why: He said he forgot the word (guessed Azan, then سجر); Amal supplied فجر.
Past 'I forgot' needs the -t ending (نسيت); he said نسي, Amal let it pass.
rows.r3_challenge: 'أنا نسي تلك الكلمة': نسيت + تلك runs t-t together, so the engine likely dropped his final ت; no voiced fix from Amal. Needs an audio check before counting as a B5 slip.

He said 'غير لو' for 'other than'; Amal: 'No لو. غير.' (ق for غ is pronunciation, not counted).

rows.medi_said: قير الشمس و اليوم شو، شو في.
rows.why: غير takes the bare noun; Amal recast without el- (again 20:30) and he asked 'قير never takes...'.
rows.english: Other than the sun and the day, what is there?

rows.medi_said: بس في الـ، الـ، الليل سما. في الليل سما،
rows.why: سما needs el- (السما) and comes first; Amal recast السما بالليل and he repeated 'الـ سما بي الليل'.
Didn't-know: Amal asked how to say 'it's dark at night', he said he forgot, she supplied عتمة (sheet 'darkness | 3etme | عتمة').
'One' follows the noun (شمس وحدة); he put it first and Amal praised the feminine without fixing the order.
noun + taani = another, agrees in gender: نجمة is feminine so تانية; Amal echoed تاني and he fixed to تانية.
Fronted object (هذي أول نجمة) needs the pointer ending; Amal prompted and he said بشوفها ('I forgot the pointer').
rows.english: This is the first star I see today.

rows.medi_said: since is لـ-لـ-lessa, right? ... Is it لا؟
rows.amal_said: No. Since-- لا is until. ... من.
rows.why: He did not know 'since' (asked لسه? لا?); Amal said no and supplied من.

rows.medi_said: آآ، بيد من because it's comparative, right?

rows.amal_said: آخر المرة means the last of the time. The end of the time. ... آخر مرة. The last time.
rows.why: aa5er + el- = 'the end of'; for 'the last time' it is آخر مرة, Amal explained and he took it.
Subject مرة is feminine so kaan must be كانت; Amal prompted 'مرة is' and he said 'feminine. كانت'.

rows.amal_said: No. ثلاث سنين الماضيين أو الماضيات would be for the last three years. ... Ago is قبل. So قبل ثلاث سنين.
rows.why: He used الماضي for 'ago'; Amal said no (that means 'the last three years'), 'ago' is قبل.
Amal recast the past form with vowels (tallajat) after his تلجات; may be only pronunciation of the doubled ل (S4) - she had said ممتاز at 35:27.

rows.why: 'The streets (in Amsterdam) are stone' takes no verb in Arabic; he built 'were made (of) stone' with عملت and Amal said just حجر: الشوارع ... حجر.

rows.r3_why: Her fix removes the verb entirely (no 'to be'), so the transcript supports grammar C1, not a vocab word swap.

rows.amal_said: تاني حجر or الحجر التاني. You said it first right.
rows.why: For 'the second stone' taani goes before the noun (or الحجر التاني); حجر تاني means 'another stone'. Amal recast and he said تاني حجر.

rows.amal_said: So you could either say my favorite stone or my favorite using عندي. المفضل عندي. ... الـ، المفضل عندي.
rows.why: 'My favorite' standing alone is المفضل عندي (adjective with el-); he said مفضل لي, Amal gave المفضل عندي and prompted 'الـ' again at 54:25 when he repeated مفضل عندي.
rows.english: the second stone was my favorite
rows.r3_why: A7 (adjective and where el- sits) covers the el- she prompted; same rule as agreed A30, so no PROPOSE needed.

rows.medi_said: I was gonna say الـ مفضل حجر.
rows.amal_said: الحجر المفضل or حجري المفضل. المفضل is an adjective.
rows.why: Adjective مفضل goes after the noun; Amal named it ('المفضل is an adjective') and gave الحجر المفضل.
A noun with a possessive ending takes no el-; Amal: 'حجري المفضل. No ال first.'

rows.amal_said: But al-mufaddal is an adjective, so it follows ders. ... هاد الدرس المفضل عندي.
rows.why: Again 'my favorite' without el-; Amal named the rule (al-mufaddal is an adjective, follows ders) and gave هاد الدرس المفضل عندي. New sentence 4 min after 54:09, so a separate row.
rows.r3_why: She named the adjective rule; A7 fits.

rows.amal_said: مش هون. مش، مش في. مش هون. ... في is not is. في is there is.
rows.why: He used في ('there is') as 'is' in 'isn't here' (engine likely merged في هون into فيهن); Amal: 'مش في. مش هون ... في is not is', and he took it ('مش هون. Okay, you're right').
rows.r3_why: Her explanation is about في wrongly standing in for 'is' (no 'to be' in Arabic) - grammar C1, not a missing word for 'here'.
